identity: An unedited Arabic student essay / free composition (school level, first-person-plural moralising register) arguing that the mobile phone and social media harm society. Three paragraphs: a hook opener naming the topic, a long body listing harms (imitation of bad fashions, family breakdown, isolation, bullying, depression, suicide, false self-image), then a short concession paragraph plus a closing exhortation with a proverb. Author-level fingerprints confirm the register: the misspelling إلي for إلى at index 43, the redundant double PP بيدهم at 4 and في أيديهم at 9, topic-chaining by bare lexical repetition (التوحد at 54 picked up as the subject التوحد والانعزال at 63), the loose feminine agreement سببت with كثرة, and the maxim close فالوقت كالسيف. This is doctrine §R (unedited student essay), not §B/§L expository nonfiction, and certainly not §M/§S/§T.
law: In §R the unit is the author's own sparse full stop, and this particular author marks it almost exclusively by ASYNDESIS: a fresh finite predication with a new subject, joined to a syntactically complete preceding clause by nothing at all. Every connective the document contains is sentence-internal by my accumulated law — حيث (B2), التي / مما (relatives), بسبب / لأن / حين / وبعد ذلك (trailing adjuncts, LAW 4), ف (LAW 2), و even with a brand-new subject (LAW 1 revised), ولكن at any length (B4). So the only positive cut cues available here are (a) <NL>, (b) a bare junction between two complete predications, and (c) the speech-act flip from description to imperative. Default is WELD (LAW 0''); I cut only where the two sides cannot be parsed as a single sentence. Measured unit in this document: 7 to 28 tokens, mean about 17, which sits just under the §R band of 20-35 because the doc is short and closes on a proverb. §R's standing warning applies throughout: these texts are UNDER-punctuated by their authors, so there are fewer boundaries than the topic structure suggests, not more.
reasoning: SITE 11 (the only genuinely uncertain one, med). A break certainly exists inside paragraph 1, because 'في أيديهم الهاتف المحمول قد يبدو كشيء عادي' cannot be read as one clause: قد يبدو needs a subject and the fronted PP would dangle. But the break is either after أيديهم (9) or after المحمول (11), and this is exactly my LAW 5 off-by-one failure mode, so I argue it rather than guess. I place it at 11. Reading في أيديهم الهاتف المحمول as a restatement clause (خبر مقدم + مبتدأ مؤخر, 'in their hands is the mobile phone') welded by a comma is the only reading that gives the otherwise glaring redundancy with بيدهم at 4 a function; it makes الهاتف المحمول the topic-naming punchline of the hook, which is how this genre opens; and it leaves قد يبدو with an idiomatic dropped subject. LAW 3 as revised also welds the apposition الهاتف المحمول backwards onto أحد أخطر الأشياء, which puts the stop after it, not before it. ولكن at 16 does not cut: B4 is emphatic that ولكن welds by default at any length and cuts only after an end-stop, and there is no end-stop at 15.  THE FIVE ASYNDETIC JUNCTIONS (45, 62, 83, 97, 146; all hi). كثرة استخدام الناس لهذه البرامج سببت (46), التوحد والانعزال ... لا مفر منه (63), زادت هذه البرامج (84), تقوم وسائل التواصل الاجتماعي (98), and كن ذكيا (147) are each a fresh finite predication with its own new subject, following a clause that is already complete, with no connective at all. Asyndesis of two full expository sentences is the one positive reason LAW 0' allows in a prose register: the author had to have typed a stop. I checked the alternative parses and all fail — كثرة cannot join the list الفساد والتهور because سببت immediately makes it a subject and 'leads to overuse of these programs' would be circular; التوحد والانعزال cannot be an apposition to ثماني ساعات; وبعد ذلك الانتحار closes the depression-to-suicide chain and cannot govern تقوم. 146/147 is the safest of the five, since it is also a speech-act flip from third-person description to second-person imperative addressed to the reader.  THE FIFTEEN DECLINED SITES, all connective-only, which is not a reason (checklist item 2): حيث at 33 — B2 was reversed in batch 2 on five documents in three registers, حيث welds; التي at 40 and مما at 91 — relative pronouns bind to their antecedents; بسبب at 55, لأنه at 72, حين at 118 and وبعد ذلك at 95 — trailing adjuncts under LAW 4, and the single known counter-example to LAW 4 was a scripture verse-index override (§M) which cannot apply to a student essay; وغير at 79 — phrase-level و joining two predicate adjectives; فتؤدي at 109 and فالوقت at 152 — LAW 2, ف is a continuation marker and now counts slightly AGAINST cutting; ويتنكر at 115 and وتساعد at 139 — و with a continuing subject; ولكنها at 131 — B4 again, and 'قد تكون لها أضرار ولكنها ساعدت' is one concessive sentence, not two; وتزيد الكراهية at 116 — this is the one I most wanted to cut, و plus a brand-new subject with its own predicate, which is the precise shape of doc_085c979b884f @489, my single most instructive false cut of batch 2, where والعقل ليس أكثر من آلة welded and the real stop came eight tokens later. I weld it. The consequence is that 98-125 is a 28-token segment, the longest in the document; I accept that, because §L/§B show 25-45-token units are normal and because every candidate split inside it is connective-driven.  THE CLOSER. 147-153 is only 7 tokens and I keep فالوقت كالسيف attached to كن ذكيا بما تفعله بوقتك. A causal ف after an imperative is written with a comma in Arabic practice, and LAW 0 as revised is explicit that a comma is not a boundary — that one clause caused about 300 of my 354 batch-2 false cuts. The proverb is the justification of the command, not a separate assertion.  POSTURE CHECK (checklist item 9). Nine boundaries: three free (23 and 125 before <NL>, 153 final), six judged. Six taken sites against fifteen declined connective sites. Not one of my cuts rests on a connective; five rest on asyndesis and one on apposition-plus-restatement. If this comes back over-cut, the culprit will be index 11 or the 45/62/83/97 asyndesis rule; if under-cut, it will be 116.
